api-docs.png.app_state: the service started from the committed model card, against the PostgreSQL that `docker compose up -d` brings up, with the ten request fixtures seeded and no prediction made yet
api-docs.png.data_source: none: the page is generated from the Pydantic models
api-docs.png.demonstrates_behaviour: the five routes and the API-key scheme are generated from the Pydantic models, so the page a caller reads cannot drift from the contract the service enforces

decision-history.png.app_state: the same service after the prediction above, so the decision log holds at least one row for employee 1
decision-history.png.data_source: the decision log this service wrote in the capture above
decision-history.png.demonstrates_behaviour: GET /history/1 returns what was decided for that employee and when, each row carrying its own threshold and model version: a past decision can be explained without guessing which model made it

prediction-logged.png.app_state: the same service, authorised in the Swagger dialog with a throwaway key, then POST /predict_by_id/1 executed from the documentation page against employee 1 of the seeded fixtures
prediction-logged.png.data_source: one of the ten fictional rows under tests/fixtures/, seeded into the employees table by scripts/db_seed_employees.py
prediction-logged.png.demonstrates_behaviour: the answer carries the threshold that turned the probability into a decision, the version of the model that produced it, and `stored: true` with the row id the decision was written to -- which is the claim this repository exists to make
